chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abi Jamiilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The merchant delays Hajj.' He said, 'He has no excuse; if he dies, he has left a pillar of the pillars of Islam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a merchant who delays Hajj without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that for a merchant, the mere accumulation of wealth or business opportunities does not constitute a valid excuse (*'udhr*) for postponing Hajj. The ruling emphasizes the urgency of the obligation, stating that dying without performing it amounts to abandoning a fundamental pillar of Islam, a view supported by Shia jurists who distinguish between temporary impediments and mere delay for worldly gain.
